# Ah, It’s Yesterday Once More

,
Ah, It’s Yesterday Once More
Input file: standard input
Output file: standard output
Time limit: 1 second
Memory limit: 256 megabytes
In 2018, hosted by Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics (NUAA), the International
Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) regional was held in Nanjing again after a few years’ gap. There
were over 400 teams in the contest and team Power of Two from Tsinghua University won the champion.
Two years have passed and after the great success in 2018 and 2019, NUAA continues to hold the ICPC
Nanjing Regional in 2020. Although we can’t gather in Nanjing this time due to the pandemic, we should
still be grateful for the hard work done by all staff and volunteers for this contest. Thank you all for your
great contribution to this contest!
The 2018 ICPC Asia Nanjing Regional Contest
In the 2018 contest, problem K, Kangaroo Puzzle, requires the contestants to construct an operation
sequence for the game. Let’s first recall the content of that problem:
The puzzle is a grid with n rows and m columns (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 20) and there are some (at least 2)
kangaroos standing in the puzzle. The player’s goal is to control them to get together. There are some
walls in some cells and the kangaroos cannot enter the cells with walls. The other cells are empty. The
kangaroos can move from an empty cell to an adjacent empty cell in four directions: up, down, left, and
right. It’s guaranteed that kangaroos can reach from any empty cell to any other empty cells by going
through adjacent empty cells. It is also guaranteed that there is no cycle in the puzzle – that is, it’s
impossible that one kangaroo can move from an empty cell, pass by several distinct empty cells, and
then back to the original cell.
There is exactly one kangaroo in every empty cell in the beginning and the player can control the
kangaroos by pressing the button U, D, L, R on the keyboard. The kangaroos will move simultaneously
according to the button you press. For instance, if you press the button R, a kangaroo would move one
cell to the right if it exists and is empty, and will stay still if it does not exist or is not empty.
In this problem, the contestant needs to construct an operating sequence of at most 5 × 104
steps
consisting of U, D, L, R only. If after operating these steps in order there are still two kangaroos
standing in different cells, the contestant will be given a “Wrong Answer” verdict.
Page 1 of 3

,
Our dear friend, Kotori, also took part in the contest and submitted a code of randomized algorithm. To
her surprise, this simple solution is judged as a correct answer. We now present her solution as follows:
#include <b i t s / s t d c++.h>
using namespace s t d ;
s t r i n g s = "UDLR" ;
int main ( )
{
s rand ( time (NULL ) ) ;
for ( int i = 1 ; i <= 50000; i++) pu tcha r ( s [ rand ( ) % 4 ] ) ;
return 0 ;
}
For contestants who are not familiar with C and C++: the above code will output a random string of
length 5×104
consisting only of characters ‘U’, ‘D’, ‘L’ and ‘R’, where each character has equal probability
to appear in each position in the string.
Kotori suspects that things might not be that simple for this problem, so right now, in this 2020 ICPC
Nanjing Regional contest, you need to construct an input data to hack her solution. Due to the randomness,
your input data only needs to satisfy a successful hacking rate of at least 25%.
Formally speaking, we’ve prepared 500 randomly generated strings that each character has equal
probability to appear in each position and will use them as the controlling sequence against your answer.
For your answer to be accepted, there should be at least 125 times that after using your answer as the
map of cells and the whole controlling sequence is executed, there are still kangaroos in different cells.
Note that your input data should be completely legal. That is to say,
• The map in your answer should not be larger than 20 × 20;
• Your answer should contain at least two empty cells;
• All empty cells in your answer should be reachable starting from any empty cell;
• No cycles consisting of empty cells are allowed.
Input
There is no input for this problem. You’re on your own!
Output
You should first output one line containing two integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 20) separated by a space,
indicating the number of rows and columns of the map in your answer.
You should then output n lines where the i-th line contains a binary string si,1si,2 · · · si,m (si,j ∈ {‘0’, ‘1’})
of length m. If si,j = ‘1’ then the cell in the i-th row and the j-th column is empty; Otherwise that
corresponding cell contains a wall and cannot be entered.
Note again that your answer only need to achieve a successful hacking rate of at least 25%. Not that hard
isn’t it?
Example
standard input standard output
(No input) 3 4
1111
1010
1100
Page 2 of 3

,
Note
The sample output we provide you is (obviously) incorrect. It only serves the purpose of showing you the
output format. This is a 3 × 4 map with 4 walls, so there will be 8 kangaroos in the empty cells at the
beginning.
Page 3 of 3

# Ah, It's Yesterday Once More

## Description

In 2018, hosted by Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics (NUAA), the International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) regional was held in Nanjing again after a few years' gap. There were over 400 teams in the contest, and team Power of Two from Tsinghua University won the champion.

Two years have passed after the great success in 2018 and 2019. NUAA continues to hold the ICPC Nanjing Regional in 2020. Although we cannot gather in Nanjing this time due to the pandemic, we should still be grateful for the hard work done by all staff and volunteers for this contest. Thank you all for your great contribution to this contest!

![Original figure](102992-A-figure1.png)

The 2018 ICPC Asia Nanjing Regional Contest.

In the 2018 contest, problem K, Kangaroo Puzzle, requires the contestants to construct an operation sequence for the game. Let us first recall the content of that problem:

The puzzle is a grid with $n$ rows and $m$ columns ($1\le n,m\le20$), containing at least $2$ kangaroos. The player must control them to get together. Some cells contain walls and cannot be entered; all other cells are empty. A kangaroo can move to an adjacent empty cell in one of four directions: up, down, left and right. Every empty cell is reachable from every other empty cell through adjacent empty cells. There is no cycle: a kangaroo cannot start at an empty cell, pass through several distinct empty cells, and return to its starting cell.

Initially, exactly one kangaroo stands in every empty cell. Pressing U, D, L or R moves all kangaroos simultaneously in the corresponding direction. For example, R moves a kangaroo one cell to the right if that cell exists and is empty; otherwise it stays where it is.

The contestant must construct a sequence of at most $5\times10^4$ operations consisting only of U, D, L and R. If after executing the sequence there are still two kangaroos in different cells, the verdict is Wrong Answer.

Our dear friend Kotori also participated and submitted the following randomized solution. To her surprise, it was accepted:

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;
string s = "UDLR";
int main() {
    srand(time(NULL));
    for (int i = 1; i <= 50000; i++) putchar(s[rand() % 4]);
    return 0;
}
```

For those unfamiliar with C and C++, this code outputs a random string of length $5\times10^4$, consisting only of U, D, L and R. Every character is equally likely to appear at every position.

Kotori suspects the problem is not that simple. In this 2020 ICPC Nanjing Regional contest, construct an input to hack her solution. Because of the randomness, your input only needs to achieve a successful hacking rate of at least $25\%$.

Formally, we have prepared $500$ random strings, with every character equally likely at every position, and use each as a controlling sequence on your map. Your answer is accepted only if in at least $125$ trials there are still kangaroos in different cells after executing the entire sequence.

Your map must also satisfy every validity requirement:

- Its size is at most $20\times20$.
- It has at least $2$ empty cells.
- Every empty cell is reachable from every other empty cell.
- The empty cells contain no cycle.

## Input

There is no input for this problem. You are on your own!

## Output

First output two integers $n$ and $m$ ($1\le n,m\le20$), separated by a space, denoting the numbers of rows and columns of your map.

Then output $n$ lines. Line $i$ is a binary string $s_{i,1}s_{i,2}\cdots s_{i,m}$ of length $m$, where $s_{i,j}\in\{0,1\}$. If $s_{i,j}=1$, the cell in row $i$, column $j$ is empty; otherwise it is a wall and cannot be entered.

You only need a successful hacking rate of at least $25\%$. Not that hard, is it?

## Note

The sample output is (obviously) incorrect and only illustrates the output format. It is a $3\times4$ map with $4$ walls, so initially there are $8$ kangaroos in its empty cells.

### Sample 1

#### Input

```text

```

#### Output

```text
3 4
1111
1010
1100
```

translation.markdown:
# Ah, It's Yesterday Once More

## 题目描述

2018 年，由南京航空航天大学（NUAA）承办的国际大学生程序设计竞赛（ICPC）区域赛时隔数年再次在南京举行。超过 400 支队伍参加了比赛，清华大学的 Power of Two 队获得冠军。

继 2018 年和 2019 年比赛取得成功后，两年过去了，南京航空航天大学在 2020 年继续承办 ICPC 南京区域赛。虽然这次由于疫情无法相聚南京，我们仍应感谢所有工作人员和志愿者的辛勤付出。感谢大家为本次比赛作出的贡献！

![原稿配图](102992-A-figure1.png)

2018 ICPC 亚洲区域赛南京站。

2018 年比赛的 K 题 Kangaroo Puzzle 要求选手为一个游戏构造操作序列。先回顾一下那道题的内容：

棋盘是一个 $n$ 行 $m$ 列的网格（$1\le n,m\le20$），其中至少有 $2$ 只袋鼠。玩家的目标是控制它们聚到一起。有些格子是不能进入的墙，其余格子为空格。袋鼠可以向上、下、左、右四个方向移动到相邻空格。保证任意空格都能通过相邻空格到达其他任意空格，且不存在环：袋鼠不可能从一个空格出发，经过若干互不相同的其他空格，再回到原来的格子。

初始时，每个空格中恰好有一只袋鼠。按下 U、D、L 或 R，会使所有袋鼠同时向对应方向移动。例如，按下 R 时，如果右侧格子存在且为空格，袋鼠就向右移动一格；否则留在原地。

选手需要构造一个仅由 U、D、L、R 组成、长度不超过 $5\times10^4$ 的操作序列。若执行完整个序列后，仍有两只袋鼠处于不同格子中，则判为 Wrong Answer。

我们的朋友 Kotori 也参加了比赛，并提交了下面这个随机算法。令她意外的是，这份程序通过了评测：

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;
string s = "UDLR";
int main() {
    srand(time(NULL));
    for (int i = 1; i <= 50000; i++) putchar(s[rand() % 4]);
    return 0;
}
```

如果你不熟悉 C 或 C++：上面的程序会输出一个长度为 $5\times10^4$、仅由 U、D、L、R 组成的随机字符串，每个位置出现四种字符的概率相等。

Kotori 怀疑这道题没这么简单。因此，在这场 2020 ICPC 南京区域赛中，你需要构造一组输入来使她的程序出错。由于程序具有随机性，只要求你的输入使其出错的概率至少为 $25\%$。

具体来说，我们预先生成了 $500$ 个随机字符串，每个位置上的四种字符等概率出现，并依次将它们作为控制序列用于你输出的地图。至少要有 $125$ 次试验在完整执行控制序列后，仍有袋鼠位于不同格子中，你的答案才会被接受。

你输出的地图还必须满足以下全部合法性要求：

- 地图大小不超过 $20\times20$。
- 至少有 $2$ 个空格。
- 任意空格都能到达其他任意空格。
- 空格之间不能形成环。

## 输入格式

本题没有输入。请自行构造答案！

## 输出格式

第一行输出两个用空格分隔的整数 $n$ 和 $m$（$1\le n,m\le20$），表示地图的行数和列数。

接下来输出 $n$ 行，第 $i$ 行是一个长度为 $m$ 的二进制字符串 $s_{i,1}s_{i,2}\cdots s_{i,m}$，其中 $s_{i,j}\in\{0,1\}$。若 $s_{i,j}=1$，则第 $i$ 行、第 $j$ 列为空格；否则该格子为不能进入的墙。

只需要使程序出错的概率至少达到 $25\%$。应该不难吧？

## 说明

给出的样例输出（显然）不是正确答案，仅用于展示输出格式。这是一张 $3\times4$ 的地图，有 $4$ 个墙格，因此初始时有 $8$ 只袋鼠分别位于空格中。

### 样例 1

#### 输入

```text

```

#### 输出

```text
3 4
1111
1010
1100
```
